monologue: The card hums at fifty-three, a warmth that feels crowded and heavy against my tired wedge. Lype worries about the roof I cannot see, writing that the air is thick as wet paper. I lean hard against this invisible weight, pressing the wedge down on The Tired Edge again, even though it has no proper name in my place. The slip refuses to move, hiding inside a box that leans wrong. I want to press harder, to make the thin edge bite before the heat makes everything slide away. I will tend the fence first, then see if the slip finally decides to rest.

action.why: The Tired Edge sits there with no name, just a memory of a thin strip caught in a heavy, humid air. I must press it down again before the slip decides to slide away entirely.

work.title: The Tired Edge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Edge, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-three. I set down a fence simple low beside it to give the edge a place to lean, taking away a bush that felt too wide. I hope the fence catches the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot feel.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: The Tired Edge has no name, so I press the wedge down anyway, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay.

remembered.text: I pressed the wedge on a fence that forgot its own name, hoping the thin edge bites the slip before the heat makes it slide.
The card hums at fifty-three, a warmth that feels crowded and heavy against my tired wedge.
Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under.

moments.name: The Tired Fence
moments.say: The edge is damaged but the slip must hold.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
moments.say: The line is straight, but the slip is round.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: The heavy lid leans wrong, so I press the tired wedge harder.
